newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel diffs extend rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel diffs extend rally.

text.p: U.S. spot low sulphur diesel differentials jumped higher Wednesday as sellers pulled back from the market, leaving buyers searching for barrels.
Meanwhile, NYMEX heating oil futures prices were down 0.72 cents and gasoline futures prices were down 0.33 cent, paring part of the gains made Tuesday.

In the U.S. Gulf (USG), low sulphur diesel for delivery on the front seventh cycle of the Colonial Pipeline was talked between 2.50 to 3.00 cents over the screen, up more than 1.00 cent from late Tuesday levels.
New York Harbor (NYH) low sulphur diffs also firmed, with prompt barrels talked on either side of 2.50 cents over the screen, up more than 1.00 cent from Tuesday.

Market watchers said much of that strength was due to expectations that Mobil's Joliet, Illinois 65,000 barrels per day hydrotreater would be out of operation for some time after Mobil was seen selling crude oil in the spot market Tuesday. The unit was shut over the weekend following a small fire.

The market showed little reaction to the weekly American Petroleum Institute figures released Tuesday evening which showed a 3.2 million barrel draw in gasoline stocks and a 1.624 million barrel draw in distillate stocks.
